title: Should the Onboarding Change Ship, Stop, or Get More Investigation?
tagline: ProductSignal: a product-journey laboratory where the experiment read is built before the dashboard. Accounts are the randomisation unit, the primary analysis is intention to treat, the sample ratio is checked before any lift is shown, the plan is frozen before any outcome is read, interim runs are labelled interim, and retention is measured on exact calendar days in the account's timezone. The known answer: 20 of 100 control accounts and 30 of 100 treatment accounts activate within seven days, a 10-point lift whose 95% interval runs from −2.0 to +21.7 points, so the result is not conclusive. Synthetic data; project 06 of the Business Data Lab.
kind: Dashboard · Product analytics · Experimentation · FastAPI · React
tech: Python 3.11 (exact rationals; Newcombe and Wilson intervals, chi-square and t quantiles without floats)
PostgreSQL 16 (append-only events, assignments unique per unit, frozen analysis plans)
FastAPI 0.162 (commands with idempotency keys, 401/403/409/422 contracts; decisions never write product state)
SQL reference recomputation of every metric
GitHub Actions (postgres:16 service, hosted runners only)
319 Python tests, 2,510 TypeScript golden and snapshot checks, 77 browser tests
note: Everything is synthetic: the 600 accounts, 1,824 users, 12,552 events, the onboarding experiment and every figure come from a seeded generator whose designed relationships and twelve injected defects are published in an injection manifest, together with the four choices its author made after looking at earlier drafts of the data (the randomisation scheme, the error model, two count tunings); everything else was drawn once and is reported as drawn. The public site is a static demo over a published snapshot; the registry and the decision screen simulate their actions in browser memory and nothing ships from them. The transactional behaviour (validating tracking, resolving identity, assigning, recording exposure, freezing a plan, analysing, reviewing guardrails, recording a decision) is verified separately on GitHub-hosted runners against a transient PostgreSQL. Built from a written specification by a coordinating session delegating bounded work to implementation subagents; not a measurement of any real product.
problem:
The onboarding experiment review argues about a dashboard. Users are counted where accounts were randomised; the result is read on day 10 of a 28-day plan and called final; a sample-ratio mismatch nobody checked sits under the lift; a cohort that signed up three days ago shows a seven-day activation rate; a segment that happened to look good is reported as the finding; and retention is one number that means exact day 7 on one page and "any time after" on another.

ProductSignal fixes the measurement first: one account-level unit, intention to treat with exposure reported beside it, the sample ratio checked before any effect is shown, a plan frozen before outcomes are read with every analysis run logged as interim or final, cohorts that only mature when their window is complete, retention measured on exact calendar days in the account's timezone, segments labelled exploratory with their multiplicity, and a decision that is ship, stop or inconclusive and never a product release.
built:
Two implementations of one contract, checked against a hand calculation and each other.

  • The contract: canonical events received by the cutoff and deduplicated, with bots, internal accounts and unknown identities excluded and counted; identity links that apply forward in time only; the account as the unit of randomisation and retention, with user events rolled up before any ratio; activation within seven days of signup on a half-open window with inclusive maturity; day-7 retention on the exact local calendar day in the account's timezone, with on-or-after-day-7 and week-4 kept separate; a versioned funnel in strict order with a maximum gap; intention to treat with the exposure rate beside it; a chi-square sample-ratio check with a verdict for too few assignments; Wilson and Newcombe intervals computed without floating point; relative lift null when the control is zero; a frozen plan whose hash every run cites; interim runs that can never support a ship; and a cutoff rule under which no assignment, exposure or subscription dated after the cutoff counts.
  • A known-answer fixture written first: 20 of 100 control and 30 of 100 treatment accounts activate, giving 0.200000 and 0.300000, +10.00 points, relative 0.500000, a Newcombe interval of −0.020249 to 0.216734 and a sample-ratio statistic of 0; a retention cohort of 20 with 5 returning on exact day 7 (two of them only because of their timezone, one returning on day 8 and so counted in on-or-after only); a funnel of 15, 10, 8 and 5; one identity link, one duplicate, one delayed event, one bot and one internal account; plus a rejected variant (an exposure before its assignment and a conflicting second assignment) and an empty variant. A standard-library script reproduces all 706 checks, including the intervals and the chi-square p-value, from the records.
  • The Python domain, PostgreSQL schema and FastAPI commands: validate tracking, resolve identity, define a funnel, assign, record exposure, freeze a plan, check maturity, analyse (sample ratio first, run logged as interim or final), review guardrails and record a decision that never changes product state; 319 tests on a GitHub-hosted runner against PostgreSQL 16, including the twelve adversarial scenarios the specification names and the cutoff rule, and an independent SQL recomputation that agrees with the domain on the fixtures and the snapshot.
  • The static site: the same contract in TypeScript with rational arithmetic only (erfc and the Student t quantile in fixed point), a journey overview with a cutoff picker, a funnel with its exclusions, a maturity-aware cohort grid in each account's timezone, an experiment result that shows the sample ratio before any lift and the generator's disclosures beside the figure, a population view of assigned versus exposed, an exploratory segment page with its multiplicity caveat and a decision memo; 2,510 golden and snapshot checks against the Python domain at six cutoffs and 77 Playwright tests at four widths and 200% zoom.
  • A deterministic synthetic world: 26 weeks, one experiment in two versions (the first with 400 accounts in permuted blocks and a true effect of eight points, the second with a designed sample-ratio mismatch), every outcome drawn once, and twelve injected defects (user-level analysis of an account-randomised test, a treatment-dependent exclusion, an interim run presented as final, an immature cohort, duplicate activations, a late event, a backward identity link, an ignored sample-ratio mismatch, cherry-picked segments, zero control conversions, exposure before assignment, mixed retention definitions) published with how each must be handled.

steps.title: The known answer before any volume
steps.body: Two cohorts of one hundred mature accounts: twenty control and thirty treatment accounts activate within seven days. Conversions 0.200000 and 0.300000, an absolute lift of 10.00 percentage points, a relative lift of 0.500000, and a Newcombe 95% interval from −2.02 to +21.67 points that crosses zero: the counts alone do not make the result conclusive, and the page says so. A standard-library script reproduces every figure, including the Wilson intervals and the chi-square sample-ratio statistic, from the records.

steps.title: Sample ratio first, then the lift
steps.body: The observed assignment counts are tested against the prespecified allocation before any effect is displayed. A mismatch is shown in place of the lift and blocks a ship decision; too few assignments to test is its own verdict rather than a pass.

steps.title: Frozen plan, labelled runs
steps.body: The primary outcome, guardrails, allocation and horizon are hashed into a frozen plan before the first analysis run. Every run cites the hash and the number of earlier runs; a run before the planned end is interim and cannot support a ship decision.

steps.title: Two modes, disclosed
steps.body: Mode A is the backend on a GitHub-hosted runner with a transient PostgreSQL. Mode B is the public site over a published snapshot; the registry and decision screens simulate their actions in browser memory and nothing ships from them.

results:
The cohort grid on the synthetic snapshot (signup weeks from 2026-04-06, each account in its own timezone, at the as-of cutoff of 2026-10-05; the week of 2026-04-13 keeps 7 of 25 accounts on exact day 7 and 16 of 25 on day 7 or later; cells whose day has not passed at the cutoff stay blank):

The experiment result on a phone:

What the data supports. The first version of the onboarding experiment assigned 400 accounts in permuted blocks of four; at its planned end 63 of 200 control and 82 of 200 treatment accounts had activated within seven days, +9.50 points (relative 0.301587) with a 95% interval from +0.08 to +18.69 points, so the final run is conclusive by a hair and the page says so beside the generator's own disclosure that the true designed effect was eight points. Week-4 retention moved −4.50 points, the guardrail error rate −0.50 points and revenue per assigned account from 97.83 to 130.95 USD, all with intervals that include zero. At the first interim cutoff only 155 accounts had been assigned (77 and 78), and the page counts only those. The second version, planned at 60/40, observed 62 control and 92 treatment assignments: a chi-square of 25.004329 with p = 0.000001, so the sample ratio is a mismatch and the result is withheld in place of a lift, blocking both ship and stop. Over the window the tracking-quality page counts 124 duplicate events dropped, 237 delayed by more than a day and 30 with an unknown identity; 69.7% of real users are linked to an anonymous visit. These are the generator's designed relationships and the one-draw realisation, published in its manifest and found by the site; they are not findings about any real product.

Not built yet: the segment page is exploratory only, no Welch interval on the revenue difference, and daylight-saving edge cases are unpinned by the fixture. The review pass by an independent reviewer is the next step on the branch.
